The U.S. reports 10 tanker aircraft operating in the region and an imminent Oman-Iran deal to reopen Hormuz navigation.

sections.executive_summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council declares the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the United States meets six explicit demands, including cessation of threats, withdrawal of forces, compensation payments, and sanctions relief. Simultaneously, NASA satellite imagery confirms a vessel fire in the strait, while Israeli forces continue striking the Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire, and an IDF soldier is wounded in an operational accident there. The U.S. has deployed ten tanker aircraft to the region and signals an imminent Oman-Iran deal to restore Hormuz transit, which would trigger a lifting of the American naval blockade on Iran.

points: Mohammad Baqer Zolghadr, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, announces the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the U.S. fulfills six conditions: cease threats and insults to sanctities; end war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen, and Iraq forever; lift the naval blockade and withdraw naval and air forces from around Iran; pay full war reparations; lift all harsh and illegal sanctions; and unconditionally release frozen and stolen Iranian assets. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/383435)

President Masoud Pezeshkian states that negotiations and expert analyses have forced the "colonialist and murderer America" to cooperate, implying diplomatic pressure is yielding results. (Source: @presstv/202020)

IRGC-affiliated media outlet Noghtezan releases imagery showing a Sayyad-2/3 surface-to-air missile transporter-erector-launcher (TEL) in the background of a relatively intact U.S. Army MQ-1C Gray Eagle drone airframe, suggesting a successful Iranian shootdown. (Source: @shin_persian/8890)
NASA satellite data detects a fire incident on a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, indicating ongoing maritime instability in the critical chokepoint. (Source: @kianmeli1/90724)

The U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctions a network of currency exchange houses and shell companies used by Iran to covertly move funds and access oil revenues, marking the eighth such action in 2026. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6150)
Israeli forces continue artillery bombardment of the Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon despite the active ceasefire agreement. (Source: @presstv/202018)

An IDF soldier suffers moderate injuries in an "operational accident" in southern Lebanon and is evacuated to a hospital; the military confirms the incident is not a security event. (Source: @manniefabian/58944)

IDF reports a terrorist infiltration alert in the West Bank settlement of Ofarim (Samaria); security forces pursue a suspicious vehicle that enters the community, the suspect exits and is apprehended after an arrest procedure involving gunfire by a security officer. (Source: @idf_telegram/24854)

A U.S. Air Force B737 (registration 02-0042, call sign SAM612) is tracked at 11,800 feet over Palestine, indicating high-level U.S. military or diplomatic movement in the theater. (Source: @redlinkleb/35361)

Open-source intelligence reports ten USAF tanker aircraft currently operating in the region, signaling sustained aerial refueling capacity for extended strike or patrol missions. (Source: @shin_persian/8887)

A Red Alert for terrorist infiltration is activated in the Samaria region at Ofarim Tzofar; IDF confirms a suspicious vehicle entered the settlement of Ofarim during a pursuit, the suspect was arrested after an armed security officer conducted a suspect arrest procedure. (Source: @tzevaadom_en/68527)

IDF details the same incident: a vehicle chased by security forces breached Ofarim, the suspect exited and was neutralized via arrest procedure including gunfire, then transferred to Judea and Samaria Police; the event is declared over with no ongoing security threat. (Source: @idf_telegram/24854)
Israeli forces persist in shelling the Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire, indicating continued kinetic activity along the Blue Line. (Source: @presstv/202018)

An IDF soldier is moderately wounded in an "operational accident" in southern Lebanon earlier today; the soldier was hospitalized and family notified; the military emphasizes it was not a combat incident. (Source: @manniefabian/58944)

Lebanese internal security apparatus RedLink launches a new reporting bot (t.me/redalertlb_twasol_bot) urging citizens to report any hostile activity including drones or warplanes to bolster the home front. (Source: @redlinkleb/35346)

In the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, Kurdish Socialist Democratic Party leader Mohammed Haji Mahmoud parades his forces in Halabja city, displaying uncontrolled weaponry in the area. (Source: @naya_foriraq/87286)

Oman's Foreign Ministry condemns repeated attacks on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz as violations of international law and threats to navigation safety, while stating ongoing negotiations on Hormuz transit arrangements are proceeding in a positive and constructive atmosphere. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/383446)
Saudi Arabia declares Iran responsible for the consequences of continued "ruthless attacks," escalating rhetorical pressure on Tehran. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/78952)

Turkish Vice President announces Saudi Arabia will provide financial support to Turkey in exchange for joint defense cooperation, signaling deepening Ankara-Riyadh military ties. (Source: @naya_foriraq/87279)

Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan sign the "Mecca Joint Defense Agreement" establishing collective deterrence against any aggressive action; an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all three. (Source: @mamlekate/104097)

CSIS assessment indicates Saudi Arabia has expended approximately 86% of its 2,800 PAC-3 missile interceptors within the first 38 days of combat, leaving only about 400 missiles in inventory as of April; other Gulf states face comparable depletion rates. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6152)

A U.S. official tells Reuters an agreement between Oman and Iran on the Strait of Hormuz is expected soon; once concluded and shipping resumes, the United States will lift its naval blockade on Iran. (Source: @asafroz/52340)

NASA satellites detect a ship fire in the Strait of Hormuz, confirming ongoing maritime incidents in the strategic waterway. (Source: @kianmeli1/90724)

IDF soldier moderately injured in a non-combat operational accident in southern Lebanon, highlighting continued troop exposure. (Source: @manniefabian/58944)

Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan formalize a tripartite mutual defense pact (Mecca Joint Defense Agreement), creating a new regional security bloc aligned against Iranian-backed threats. (Source: @mamlekate/104097)
sections.threat_assessment: Iran's closure ultimatum for the Strait of Hormuz, backed by six maximalist demands, raises the risk of a major maritime confrontation if the U.S. does not comply or negotiate. The confirmed vessel fire in the strait underscores the fragility of energy transit. Israel's continued strikes in Lebanon despite the ceasefire suggest either enforcement of a buffer zone or deliberate provocation, while the IDF's operational accident reveals sustained troop presence in hostile terrain. The display of a downed U.S. MQ-1C by Iranian air defenses signals improved Iranian SAM capability and willingness to publicize successes. Saudi PAC-3 depletion to ~400 interceptors indicates severe air defense attrition, potentially inviting further missile or drone attacks on Gulf infrastructure. The new Saudi-Turkish-Pakistani defense pact creates a Sunni-led military coalition that could coordinate against Iranian proxies, altering regional deterrence dynamics.
sections.regional_response: Oman positions itself as a mediator, condemning Hormuz attacks while reporting constructive navigation talks, and a U.S. official anticipates an imminent Oman-Iran deal that would trigger a U.S. naval blockade lift. Saudi Arabia escalates rhetoric, holding Tehran accountable for "ruthless attacks" and formalizing a collective defense treaty with Turkey and Pakistan that explicitly treats an attack on one as an attack on all. Turkey leverages the pact to secure Saudi financial backing for joint defense. The U.S. maintains heavy tanker presence and high-value aerial assets (SAM612 over Palestine), signaling readiness for extended operations. Meanwhile, the U.S. Treasury intensifies financial pressure on Iran's oil revenue networks with its eighth sanctions package in 2026.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Sayyad-2/3 TEL appearance alongside an intact MQ-1C airframe in IRGC-released imagery is a deliberate signal of Iranian air defense proficiency and intelligence exploitation of captured U.S. technology. The SNSC's 160-day reference to public chants of the six demands suggests a coordinated domestic mobilization campaign to legitimize the Hormuz closure. Saudi PAC-3 exhaustion rates (86% in 38 days) imply either intense Houthi/Iranian missile volume or potential data exaggeration; either way, Gulf air defense sustainability is a critical vulnerability. The Mecca Joint Defense Agreement's Article 5-style clause marks a significant shift from bilateral to multilateral Gulf security architecture, potentially enabling Turkish military deployments to the Peninsula. The U.S. B737 (SAM612) over Palestine may indicate senior leader travel or command-and-control relay for regional operations.
